content:
maria: Heads up — since the APAC GPU shuffle at 03:10 UTC we've started losing a bunch of runtime spans in traces for large-context requests. Observability link: https://grafana.redwood/infinity/d/trace/trace-overview (APAC filter).

kai: I see. Most traces only have ingress + gateway spans. runtime-worker spans (token generation) are absent. Prom shows no CPU spike but GPU memory OOMs on some pods.

ash: Are we sure those requests hit the dedicated GPU nodes and not hitting fallback cheap models?

maria: They should be pinned to the large-run pool. The rollout moved 3 pods between zones and the autoscaler drained a node. Node drain logs: 
```
kubelet: Evicting pod redwood-runtime-llm-7cbf OOMKilled
kernel: out_of_memory: Kill process 12345 (python) score 987
```

jordan: If the process dies during generation, runtime won't emit final spans. But we still expect a partial runtime span (start) with end timestamp. We're seeing zero runtime spans. That suggests the tracer context isn't making it from gateway to runtime.

kai: Good call. I grep'd logs for `traceparent` and `otlp` headers at the gateway layer. Many requests are missing trace headers when forwarded to the runtime: `traceparent: -` in proxy logs.

maria: That would explain pure ingress-only traces. Why would headers drop during node drain? Maybe the sidecar proxy was restarted and lost in-flight headers?

ash: Also check the envoy x-forwarded-* behavior. We recently changed the internal LB to terminate TLS and reconnect to pods; headers might be stripped unless `preserve_host_header` is set.

kai: I dumped a request sample: 
```
Gateway -> Envoy ingress -> LB -> NodePort -> runtime-pod
Headers at Gateway: traceparent: 00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01
Headers at runtime: traceparent: <missing>
```

maria: So the trace context is being dropped by the LB/Envoy hop. We need to ensure OTLP/traceparent propagation across all proxies and also that the otel sdk is configured to accept `traceparent` from upstream.

jordan: On top of that, when pods OOM, the collector's exporter buffer gets reset — we might lose open spans in memory. Two separate loss modes: (1) header drop meaning no runtime spans associated with trace, (2) runtime crash before flush. Both observed.

sre-bot: Alert triggered: `trace-prop-drop-rate` (apac) > 15% for 10m. Incident channel: #incidents.

maria: Suggested immediate mitigations: add header whitelist in Envoy to preserve `traceparent`, throttle node drains during high GPU utilization, and set otel sdk to sync flush on SIGTERM to give process time to export spans.

ash: For Envoy, add to the cluster config: 
```
request_headers_to_add:
  - header: { key: "traceparent", value: "%REQ(traceparent)%" }
```
But if LB rewrites headers we also need `preserve_external_request_id`.

kai: For SIGTERM flush, add to runtime container: `OTEL_BSP_MAX_EXPORT_BATCH_SIZE=1` and `OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER=parentbased_traceidratio` temporarily to favor flushing. Also ensure graceful termination has 30s preStop sleep.

jordan: We should avoid full sampling change long-term — that explodes costs. Instead implement adaptive sampling: always sample 100% for `customer_tier=premium` or `model=/gptx-large` and 1% for background rerank routes. That gives us critical traces for debugging while keeping cost down.

maria: Agree. Also add a quick correlation between Prom metrics and traces: create a Grafana panel that shows `trace_drop_rate` alongside `gpu_pod_oom_total` and `kube_node_drains`.

grafana-bot: New panel created: "APAC trace drop vs GPU OOM" in team dashboard. Link: https://grafana.redwood/d/apac/trace-drop-gpu-oom

kai: One tricky bit: our trace gateway performs fanout to multiple collectors and will drop the header if max header size > 8kb (some clients pass baggage). We should limit baggage via sdk config: `OTEL_BAGGAGE_MAX_SIZE=512`.

ash: Also check our OTLP gateway sampling rules — it currently applies head-based sampling before route enrichment; we should apply attribute enrichment (attach model_id, customer_tier) earlier so the sampler can make informed decisions.

maria: I pushed a small hotfix to the envoy config with header preserve and increased preStop to 30s. Deploy bot: please roll to APAC small first.

deploy-bot: roll started: rollout/id=rn-2026-03-apac-trace-preserve - step 1/3 -> staging-apac-small
deploy-bot: rollout succeeded step 1/3
deploy-bot: step 2/3 -> canary-apac-large
deploy-bot: step 2/3 succeeded

kai: After canary I see `traceparent` preserved on forwarded requests. Trace drop rate dropped from 18% -> 4% in the canary cluster.

maria: Nice. Next actions: 
- infra: enforce graceful termination and adjust autoscaler to avoid draining during peak inference windows (kai)
- runtime: add SIGTERM sync flush + reduced BSP batch size in runtime image (ash)
- platform: implement attribute-first enrichment in gateway so sampler can use model/customer tags (jordan)
- observability: add dashboard panels and alert rule tuned to trace_drop_rate by route/model (maria)

ash: I'll open PRs for the runtime changes — include a small test harness to simulate OOM flush behavior.

jordan: I'll prototype attribute enrichment in a sidecar that tags requests from gateway with `x-redwood-model` before sampling.

maria: Thanks all. Can we reconvene in 2 hours to validate metrics after APAC rollout completes? :hourglass_flowing_sand:

kai: ack. Will monitor `trace-prop-drop-rate` and `gpu_pod_oom_total`.

sre-bot: Follow-up reminder in 2h: check APAC trace-drop reduction.
